capabilities.title: Which coding agents are supported, at what integration depth
Whether the product speaks a structured transport rather than wrapping a terminal
Separate accounts, profiles and config homes
Quota, usage and rate-limit visibility and switching
Parallel work in isolated worktrees or branches
Named agent or teammate identity that survives a harness change
Task or objective hierarchy, delegation and handoffs
Completion, review and verification behaviour, and how much is deterministic
Durable specification artifacts rather than transcript
Artifact identity, versioning, handoff and review semantics
Codebase knowledge with provenance, freshness and traceability
Terminals, diffs and files inside the product
Preview or browser surface tied to the work
Voice, dictation or routines on an agent
Mobile or remote control of a running session
Local-first or cloud-dependent hosting and data ownership

claims.observation: Every task gets its own git worktree, its own agent terminal and its own browser

evidence.excerpt: Orca is a desktop IDE for running multiple AI coding agents side by side. Every task gets its own git worktree, its own agent terminal, and its own browser

claims.observation: Runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi side by side, one CLI agent per worktree terminal

evidence.excerpt: The AI Orchestrator for 100x builders. Run Codex, ClaudeCode, OpenCode or Pi side-by-side — each in its own worktree, tracked in one place.

claims.observation: Terminals, diffs, a browser and a CLI ship in the product

evidence.excerpt: Run Claude Code, Codex, and any other coding agent in parallel, each in its own worktree. Terminals, diffs, a browser, and a CLI, in one app built for agents.
